entities.name: Liberal Party of Andorra
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Liberal Party of Andorra, founded in 1992, emerged as a significant political force in the microstate of Andorra, located in the Eastern Pyrenees between France and Spain. As a center-right political party, it has played a crucial role in shaping contemporary Andorran politics, promoting liberal and progressive policies that align with European norms and values. Key figures associated with its formation include former Prime Minister Antoni Martí, who led the party during its early years and helped establish a platform that sought to modernize Andorra's economy and public governance, reflecting broader trends in Southern European politics.

Since its inception, the Liberal Party has participated in numerous elections, gaining substantial representation in the General Council, Andorra's parliament. The party's notable achievements include advocating for tax reforms, improving public services, and enhancing civil liberties. Its influence peaked during the 2011 elections when it formed a coalition government, marking a shift towards a more open and transparent political framework in Andorra. The party's policies often emphasized the importance of integration with European institutions, steering Andorra towards greater alignment with EU standards.

The legacy of the Liberal Party can be seen in its lasting impact on Andorrean society, contributing to a gradual transformation of the political landscape from a historically conservative paradigm. By championing liberal values, the party has fostered a more dynamic civil society and encouraged citizen engagement in governance. This shift has influenced subsequent political parties and movements, leading to a more pluralistic and vibrant political discourse in Andorra. The party's establishment also coincided with a broader trend of democratization in microstates across Europe, reflecting the changing nature of governance in the region.
